title: Quota fallthrough simulation lab — sprint 0 notes
content:
Goal: exercise our quota fallthrough path under realistic traffic shapes and quantify the impact on latency, error rates, and auth fallback frequency.

Background/context:
- Motivation: observed transient hotspots where token-bucket quotas hit unexpectedly, causing routing to fall back to lower-tier capacity. We need to understand behavior across control plane routing, auth token validation latencies, and quota reassignment.
- Scope for sprint 0: synthetic simulation only (no prod traffic replay). Focus on three vectors: bursty short requests (chat), long seq generation (>=2k tokens), and mixed embed-heavy bursts.

Environment and tooling:
- Simulation harness: ./tools/quota-sim v0.9 (python) running on staging-k8s-nodes (type: rtx-a2-small), 8 workers.
- Config used: experiments/2026-01/quota-fallthrough-config.yaml (attached in linked_artifacts). Key params: global_bucket=1000 rps, per-customer-bucket=200 rps, soft_shrink_pct=0.25, fallback_targets=[dedicated-s1, hosted-lowprio].
- Tracing: open-telemetry traces forwarded to jaeger-staging; use trace tags: sim.run=quota-fallthrough-01.
- Metrics captured: request_latency_p50/p95, error_rate_5m, auth_latency_ms, routing-fallthrough-count, fallback_success_rate.

Summary of runs (high-level):
- Run A (bursty chat): 10k total requests over 5m, 60% short (<160 tokens), 40% medium. Observed routing-fallthrough-count=312 (3.1%). p95 latency increased from 85ms -> 210ms for affected requests. Auth latency for fallthrough path median +50ms.
- Run B (long gen): 2k long requests (>2k tokens). Routing fallthrough triggered 12% of requests. End-to-end token throughput dropped ~18% on hosted lane but dedicated-s1 absorbed ~70% of fallback traffic. Noted increased KV-cache misses in fallback models.
- Run C (mixed embed spikes): short spike bursts (500 rps peak for 30s). Very few fallthroughs (0.4%) but when occurred, error_rate_5m spiked to 2.3% for those customer buckets (mostly 429s).

Interesting observations / anomalies:
- Auth token validation: a 200ms spike in token validation (dependent on auth service DNS TTL refresh) correlated with a 20% increase in fallthroughs for Run A. Hypothesis: transient auth latency increases cause timeout-driven routing fallback.
- Sticky routing bias: some customers with pinning to hosted model variants experienced repeated fallthrough due to conservative backoff timers; our current backoff algorithm is too simplistic when combined with token-bucket replenishment windows.
- Fallback model capacity reporting lag: dedicated pool metrics were delayed ~45s during peak simulation which caused double-routing (requests sent to fallback and retried to origin) — leads to over-subscription.
- KV cache warming: fallback to smaller quantized models results in higher KV-cache miss rates; this increased overall token compute time by ~12% in Run B.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Maya: add short-circuit in routing when auth latency > 150ms to avoid cascading fallthroughs (proposal sketch in PR). ETA: 2026-01-22.
- Omar: adjust per-customer token-bucket window to be jittered across 10s to avoid synchronized refill (experiment change). ETA: 2026-01-18.
- Claire: instrument dedicated pool capacity reporting to emit heartbeat metric every 5s and add alert if metrics lag > 10s. ETA: 2026-01-20.
- Diego: run a follow-up sim with prod-replay shapes for top-50 customers to validate changes. ETA: 2026-01-28.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is the auth service DNS TTL refresh behavior acceptable? Should we add client-side caching of token validation endpoints? (Ongoing conversation with security team)
- Should fallback routes avoid models with large KV-cache penalties for long-gen workloads? Need cost tradeoff analysis.
- How to expose customer-level fidelity in routing decisions without leaking cross-tenant metrics (privacy).

Quick commands and artifacts used during sim (notes for reproducibility):
- Start sim: python tools/quota-sim/run.py --config experiments/2026-01/quota-fallthrough-config.yaml --tag quota-fallthrough-01
- Trace lookup: jaeger-staging/search?trace=sim.run=quota-fallthrough-01
- Prom query examples: rate(routing_fallthrough_count[1m]) by (target_pool)

Decisions made in meeting:
- Short-term: implement jittered refill windows + heartbeat metric for pool reporting. Both are low-risk and should reduce synchronized fallthroughs.
- Mid-term: prototype routing heuristic that factors in auth latency signal; only trigger if sustained > 10s. Evaluate risk of false positives.

Notes to follow-up meeting:
- Compare metrics after jitter + heartbeat in next sim. Aim to reduce average fallthrough from ~3% -> <1% for bursty traffic.
- Prepare a short playbook for on-call containing: how to identify quota fallthrough incidents, quick mitigations (increase per-customer bucket temporarily, disable fallback to specific pools), and when to escalate. Draft due 2026-01-25 (owner: Maya).

Raw sample trace snippet (abridged):
- trace_id: 0x9a3f... -> auth.validate token (120ms) -> routing.decide (12ms) -> fallback.enqueue -> model.load (220ms) -> response (450ms)

Misc notes (brainstorm fragments):
- Could we pre-warm fallback model kv-cache for high-risk customers based on predicted fallthrough probability? (warm cache would cost tokens but save latency in long-run)
- Use lightweight probabalistic feature to avoid full fallback — e.g., redirect 5% to fallback as probe and escalate if probe cost acceptable.

If you worked on a section, paste your snippet/notes below (quick capture):
- Omar (notes): added jitter param, ran quick smoke with 3 workers, saw immediate defrag of refill alignment. Details: experiments/2026-01/jitter-smoke-01.log
- Claire (notes): heartbeat metric implemented in pool-exporter, initial PR open at runtime/pull/1423; needs load test.
- Diego (notes): preparing prod-replay subset, pulling top-50 customers from billing export for realistic shapes.

Next sync: quick 30m sync Wed 2026-01-20 10:00 PST to review sim results and decide whether to roll jitter/heartbeat to canary.

End of doc.
